title: Forming the Feminine Colour, اسْم الْجِنْس, مَا الْمَوْصُولَة against الَّذِي, and a First Look at لَام التَّعْلِيل
summary: Homework on the new verb patterns is reviewed from the Qur'ān, then the class derives the feminine colour mechanically — drop the opening hamza, add alif and hamza at the end — giving خَضْرَاء from أَخْضَر and سَمْرَاء from أَسْمَر. Along the way the teacher explains اسْم الْجِنْس, the collective noun behind شَجَر against شَجَرَة, draws the line between مَا الْمَوْصُولَة and الَّذِي, and closes with a preview of لَام التَّعْلِيل, the lām that gives a reason and puts the following verb into the accusative.
key_points: To form a feminine colour from the masculine, remove the hamza at the front and add an alif and hamza at the end: أَخْضَر becomes خَضْرَاء, أَسْمَر becomes سَمْرَاء — giving the set حَمْرَاء، سَوْدَاء، بَيْضَاء، صَفْرَاء، خَضْرَاء، سَمْرَاء.
The teacher's broader point: Arabic is largely a matter of patterns, and once you can recognise a pattern and fit words onto it, much of the language opens up.
A colour is a صِفَة, so it follows its noun in both gender and case: قَلَمًا أَصْفَرَ takes the fatḥa because قَلَمًا does; بِالْقَلَمِ الْأَحْمَرِ takes the kasra for the same reason.
لِحْيَة (beard) is feminine, so it takes a feminine colour — لِحْيَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ — while شَعْر (hair) is masculine.

اسْم الْجِنْس (ism al-jins : the collective noun) names a category. شَجَر is trees in general and is masculine; شَجَرَة is one tree and is feminine — hence الشَّجَرِ الْأَخْضَرِ but شَجَرَةٌ خَضْرَاءُ. The same holds for نَمْل and نَمْلَة.
A collective noun is not a plural — the plural of شَجَرَة is أَشْجَار — but its meaning is effectively plural, in the way إِنْسَان can stand for humankind as a category rather than one person.
آخَر is غَيْر مُنْصَرِف and so carries no tanwīn: آخَرُ, not آخَرٌ. Its feminine is أُخْرَى.
مَا الْمَوْصُولَة and الَّذِي both mean that or which, but they differ in scope: الَّذِي may be used for عَاقِل — people, and Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ — whereas مَا is used only for غَيْر عَاقِل.
The three types of مَا, now complete: الِاسْتِفْهَامِيَّة, learned in the very first lesson of Book One as مَا هَذَا; النَّافِيَة, which negates; and الْمَوْصُولَة, meaning that which.

لَام التَّعْلِيل (lām al-taʿlīl) is the lām that states the reason behind an action, and it puts the following مُضَارِع into the accusative with a fatḥa: خَرَجْتُ لِأَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ, I went out so that I could drink water; خَرَجَ لِيَغْسِلَ وَجْهَهُ, he went out to wash his face. Note أَشْرَبَ and يَغْسِلَ rather than the usual أَشْرَبُ and يَغْسِلُ.
الْقُبَّة is the Arabic for a dome, the word behind the Urdu gumbad — as in الْقُبَّة الْخَضْرَاء.
Vocabulary: شَعْر (hair), لِحْيَة (beard), مِنْدِيل (handkerchief), مِلَفّ (folder), طَبَاشِير (chalk), غَائِب (absent), and هَاتِ with its forms هَاتِي، هَاتُوا، هَاتِينَ.
questions: [00:19:00] Q: Why is it الشَّجَرِ الْأَخْضَرِ in one place but شَجَرَةٌ خَضْرَاءُ in another? — A: شَجَر is the collective, treated as masculine; شَجَرَة is a single tree and is feminine. The same pattern appears with نَمْل and نَمْلَة in the story of Sulaymān عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام.
[00:20:01] Q: Is شَجَر the plural of شَجَرَة? — A: No; the plural is أَشْجَار. شَجَر is an اسْم الْجِنْس, naming the category, though its sense comes out as plural.
[00:22:00] Q: How do you make a colour feminine? — A: Drop the hamza from the front and add an alif and hamza at the end: أَسْمَر gives سَمْرَاء.
[00:27:01] Q: Why do both words carry a fatḥa there? — A: Because the colour is the صِفَة of a noun that is مَنْصُوب, and a صِفَة matches its noun in case.
[00:29:00] Q: What is a dome called in Arabic? — A: الْقُبَّة — the source of the Urdu word gumbad.
[00:34:01] Q: What is مَا الْمَوْصُولَة? — A: It means that or which, like الَّذِي, but with one restriction: مَا is used only for غَيْر عَاقِل, never for people or for Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ.
[00:36:00] Q: What are the three kinds of مَا again? — A: الِاسْتِفْهَامِيَّة from the very first lesson of Book One, النَّافِيَة for negation, and الْمَوْصُولَة for that which.
[00:39:00] Q: What does لَام التَّعْلِيل do to the verb after it? — A: It puts it into the accusative with a fatḥa — لِأَشْرَبَ, لِيَغْسِلَ — instead of the usual ḍamma.

quiz.q: How is the feminine of أَخْضَر formed?
options: By adding a tāʾ marbūṭah: أَخْضَرَة
By dropping the opening hamza and adding alif and hamza: خَضْرَاء
quiz.a: The mechanical rule the teacher gave, producing حَمْرَاء، سَوْدَاء، بَيْضَاء، صَفْرَاء، خَضْرَاء، سَمْرَاء.

quiz.q: Why does the colour in بِالْقَلَمِ الْأَحْمَرِ carry a kasra?
options: Because colours always take a kasra
Because it is the صِفَة of a noun that is مَجْرُور
quiz.a: A صِفَة matches its noun in case, and الْقَلَم is مَجْرُور after the بَاء.

options: A noun naming a category, whose sense is effectively plural
quiz.a: شَجَر means trees in general, as إِنْسَان can stand for humankind — not a plural in form, but plural in sense.

quiz.q: Which is the single tree, and which gender does it take?
quiz.a: شَجَرَة is one tree and is feminine, hence شَجَرَةٌ خَضْرَاءُ; the collective شَجَر is masculine.

quiz.q: What is the plural of شَجَرَة?
quiz.a: The teacher was explicit that the plural is أَشْجَار, and that شَجَر is something different — a collective.

quiz.q: Why does آخَر never take tanwīn?
quiz.a: It belongs to the diptote category, so it is آخَرُ rather than آخَرٌ.

quiz.q: What is the difference in use between مَا الْمَوْصُولَة and الَّذِي?
options: مَا is only for غَيْر عَاقِل; الَّذِي may also be used for people and for Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ
الَّذِي is only for the plural
مَا is only used in questions
quiz.a: This was the refinement the teacher added: both mean that which, but مَا is restricted to what lacks intellect.

options: The reason or purpose behind an action
quiz.a: From تَعْلِيل, giving a cause: خَرَجْتُ لِأَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ, I went out in order to drink water.

quiz.q: What does لَام التَّعْلِيل do to the verb following it?
quiz.a: أَشْرَبُ becomes لِأَشْرَبَ and يَغْسِلُ becomes لِيَغْسِلَ.
لِحْيَة is feminine, so the colour takes its feminine form — لِحْيَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ.

quran_examples.arabic: تُرِيدُونَ عَرَضَ الدُّنْيَا وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ
quran_examples.transliteration: turīdūna ʿaraḍa al-dunyā wa-llāhu yurīdu al-ākhirah
quran_examples.translation: You desire the commodities of this world, while Allah desires the Hereafter.
quran_examples.note: A student's homework answer, and the teacher noted it gives two forms of أَرَادَ، يُرِيدُ at once — تُرِيدُونَ and يُرِيدُ — on the أَفْعَلَ pattern introduced last session.

quran_examples.arabic: أَوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم ۚ بَلَىٰ
quran_examples.transliteration: a-wa-laysa alladhī khalaqa al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa bi-qādirin ʿalā an yakhluqa mithlahum, balā
quran_examples.translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes indeed.
quran_examples.note: Included for الَّذِي used of Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ — the contrast the teacher drew, since مَا الْمَوْصُولَة could never be used this way.

quran_examples.arabic: الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ الشَّجَرِ الْأَخْضَرِ نَارًا فَإِذَا أَنتُم مِّنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ
quran_examples.transliteration: alladhī jaʿala lakum mina al-shajari al-akhḍari nāran fa-idhā antum minhu tūqidūn
quran_examples.translation: It is He who made for you from the green tree fire, and from it you kindle.
quran_examples.note: الشَّجَر here is the collective اسْم الْجِنْس, taking the masculine الْأَخْضَر — set against شَجَرَةٌ خَضْرَاءُ for a single tree.

quran_examples.arabic: حَتَّىٰ إِذَا أَتَوْا عَلَىٰ وَادِ النَّمْلِ قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ
quran_examples.transliteration: ḥattā idhā ataw ʿalā wādi al-namli qālat namlatun yā ayyuhā al-namlu dkhulū masākinakum
quran_examples.translation: Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said: O ants, enter your dwellings.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's parallel case: النَّمْل as the collective, but قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ with the feminine verb for one ant. The āyah also carries the plural command اُدْخُلُوا from the imperative lessons.

quran_examples.translation: It is a yellow cow, bright in colour.
quran_examples.note: Recalled again as the clearest Qur'ānic instance of the feminine colour pattern فَعْلَاء agreeing with its noun.

quran_examples.arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-mā khalaqtu al-jinna wa-l-insa illā li-yaʿbudūn
quran_examples.translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.
quran_examples.note: A Qur'ānic instance of لَام التَّعْلِيل, the lām of purpose previewed at the end of the session; it also opens with مَا النَّافِيَة negating a مَاضِي verb.

quran_examples.arabic: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ
quran_examples.transliteration: laqad khalaqnā al-insāna fī aḥsani taqwīm
quran_examples.translation: We have certainly created man in the best of stature.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's analogy for اسْم الْجِنْس: الْإِنسَان is singular in form but means humankind as a category, not one individual. أَحْسَن here is also an اسْم التَّفْضِيل as a مُضَاف, giving the superlative.
